reason: I want to build a stable place to sit and work, and the bricks and metal seem useful for its structure.
expectation: I expect them to form a bench or other support, though I do not know its exact shape.

alternatives.reason: The felt and fabric could make a cushion, but I want to make the supporting structure first.

effect: The bricks and metal made the bench and worktop, so the remaining felt and fabric may make it more comfortable.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the same materials used to make a place by the window.
reason: This is the only available combination, and the felt and fabric seem suited to cushioning the bench.
expectation: I expect to make a cushion or covering, though I do not know exactly how it will be used.

effect: The felt and fabric made a cushion, ready to fit onto the bench.
reaction: The result was as expected; nothing else stood out.
reason: This is the only available combination, and putting the cushion on the bench should finish the seat.
expectation: I expect a cushioned window bench and possibly completion of the seating goal.

effect: The cushion completed the window bench and fulfilled the chapter’s goal, giving the cabin a place to sit and work.
reaction: The image of watching the sunset from the padded seat is a satisfying finish.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the bench structure was most worthwhile: it reused familiar materials for a practical place beside the window.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the cushion was straightforward and had little to discover on its own.

surprise.text: The bench also included a worktop; I had expected a seat or support but did not know its shape.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary. The materials and their uses were clear, though the last two combinations were the only available actions.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, out of curiosity about how life on Mars develops beyond these practical preparations.
